A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ensemble++ research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched despite retitling, rewriting, and layout changes.

before.justification: V4 reports original bandit simulations, UCI benchmark evaluations, language-model content-moderation results, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V5 retains original experimental outcomes, including regret and accuracy curves for linear, nonlinear, UCI, and content-moderation tasks, together with ablation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 7 adds the missing sqrt(M/s) factor to sparse-sampling pseudocode, aligning it with Definition E.4 already present in v4. This is a limited procedural correction; the shared-factor updates, neural architecture, objectives, and main algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate finite- and compact-action linear bandits, quadratic and vector-quadratic bandits, neural bandits, UCI Mushroom and Shuttle, and hate-speech moderation. The GPT-2 and Pythia experiments were already present in v4.

E2.justification: Corresponding empirical comparisons retain TS, ensemble sampling/RRLS, Ensemble+, EpiNet, Greedy, and LMCTS. EpiNet remains excluded from hate-speech detection. The comparator substitution in Table 2 concerns theoretical research positioning.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated finite-action sampling range from [-1/sqrt(5), 1/sqrt(5)]^d to [-1/sqrt(d), 1/sqrt(d)]^d. However, v5 Appendix F.1 retains the former range. This is a reported setting revision with an internal inconsistency, without evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The distribution and ensemble-size sweeps, action-set scaling, buffer-capacity ablation, and frozen-versus-finetuned language-model studies are retained. V4 Figure 5(b)'s buffer analysis moves to v5 Figure 15; it is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains 200 repetitions for linear experiments and 10 distinct random seeds for nonlinear experiments. The matched empirical figures preserve their uncertainty displays; no new statistical estimation or significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: Matched empirical curves, heatmaps, bars, and findings are retained. The minimum-ensemble-size fits still report R-squared values of 0.98 and 0.93, and Section 5.2 retains the reported 5% hate-speech advantage over Ensemble+. Figure rearrangements do not establish changed outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 replaces the stated regret expression and changes its probability guarantee from 1−delta to 1−2delta. Appendix D adds explicit regret derivations and revises the optimism argument, including a threshold change from 1 to sqrt(2). Appendices C and E also correct formal conditions and sparse-distribution reasoning. These changes go beyond expanded exposition.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a shared ensemble factor, approximately d log T ensemble size, TS-comparable linear regret across the four action/context settings, and a neural extension with favorable empirical scalability. V5 emphasizes these claims more explicitly, but their substantive scope was already present in v4.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly acknowledges Ensemble++'s O(d^3 log T) linear update cost versus exact TS's O(d^3), arguing that the overhead supports extension to non-conjugate models. This adds a substantive qualification to the efficiency interpretation. The principal empirical interpretations and appendix limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly supplies a substantial training recipe, including M=8, batch size 128, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 0.01, buffer capacity 10,000, and task-specific gradient-step counts. Conversely, v4's task-specific CPU/P40/V100 disclosure and Ensemble+/EpiNet implementation-source links disappear. The Ensemble++ code link is relocated, not newly introduced.

R1.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 replace the Janz et al. comparison with Lee and Oh (2024), revising the discussion of ensemble-size and regret advantages. Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984) and Vershynin (2012) are also added. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title becomes Scalable Exploration via Ensemble++. The abstract, contributions, background, and theoretical narrative receive extensive rewriting; Appendices C–D are substantially reorganized and expanded. V5 also adds contents pages and removes the standalone Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. V4 Figures 2–3 merge into v5 Figure 2, the nonlinear comparison changes from a 2-by-2 arrangement to four horizontal panels, and the buffer plot moves to the appendix. Table 2 gains an ensemble-size column, and Table 5 newly summarizes existing distribution properties.

improvement.justification: V5 adds useful training settings and clearer navigation, but its expanded theory does not reliably resolve v4's proof deficiencies. Revised Proposition D.6 incorrectly transfers a probability lower bound at threshold 1 to sqrt(2), while new Equation (39) reverses the determinant ratio for the shrinking covariance. V4 already had inconsistent inflation factors and an incomplete final derivation. These formal problems, together with v5's conflicting sampling ranges, leave the net effect of the documentation gains and technical regressions uncertain.
